payload.name: Expand item-list searches to related activity terms
payload.description: When a question asks for a list of named items (e.g., music pieces, tracks, albums) tied to a person's routine activity (e.g., yoga), before answering, also search with closely related activity terms (e.g., meditation, relaxation) and include relevant results.
content: For enumerative questions asking for named items a person uses during an activity, run at least one additional search using closely related activity terms (e.g., yoga → meditation, relaxation; workout → exercise, training) alongside the exact activity.
If the additional search returns memories mentioning the same person and the same item category, include them in evidence and answer; then stop—do not keep expanding to unrelated terms.

Do not apply when the question asks for a single fact (e.g., 'What is her favorite yoga track?') or when the related-activity search returns nothing relevant; answer from the initial evidence in those cases.

solves: The general failure is answering an enumerative question with an incomplete list because retrieval was restricted to the exact activity named in the question. This applies to future questions asking for named items (e.g., music, tracks, albums) a person uses during a routine activity, where related activity terms (e.g., meditation for yoga) can surface additional stored items. It must not apply to questions seeking a single fact or when the exact-activity search already covers the answer.
